claim.pdf_says: feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2 / device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3 appear EXACTLY ONCE on the page, as the second and third alternatives INSIDE the switch-name-1 outer bracket of the SPECIAL-NAMES diagram. They are not printed anywhere else.
claim.markdown_says: ISO_COBOL.md lines 13937-13938 correctly place them inside the diagram, and then lines 13944-13945 print them AGAIN as two free-standing code spans after the figure notes: `feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2` / `device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3`
claim.why_it_matters: The duplicate copies sit at the same indentation level as the genuine top-level SPECIAL-NAMES clauses ([ symbolic-characters-clause ] ... on line 13947, [ ORDER TABLE ... ] . on line 13949). A reader - or a grammar generator - walking the SPECIAL-NAMES clause list will read them as two additional mandatory, unbracketed top-level clauses, when in fact they are alternatives inside an optional repeatable group.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered PDF page (E:/Temp/specrecon/v320/spec_p320.png, 2550x3300 @300dpi, printed folio 290) and of specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 13930-13949 (work-unit slice starts at md_source_line 13897, so the whole 12.3.7.2 General format block is inside page 320 - no page-boundary spillover to explain a second copy).

WHAT THE PRINTED PAGE SHOWS. I cropped and magnified the bottom of the switch-name-1 figure (x 200-2000, y 2130-2560) and read the glyphs. Below the second alternative's brace group the page prints, in order:
  (a) a vertical bracket stroke, then 'feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2';
  (b) the outer bracket's bottom-left corner glyph (the lower foot of the tall left bracket), then 'device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3' - the matching bottom-right corner of the tall right bracket sits on the same baseline at the far right, closing the group;
  (c) '[ symbolic-characters-clause ] ...' starting at the normal left margin, with NO enclosing tall bracket;
  (d) '[ ORDER TABLE ordering-name-1 IS literal-9 ] .' - the terminating period of the SPECIAL-NAMES format;
  (e) nothing further but the folio '290  (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license footer.
So each of the two phrases is printed once and only once on the page, and both are unambiguously inside the tall outer bracket that also encloses switch-name-1 (the same bracket that carries the trailing ellipsis at its right). There is no second, unbracketed printing of either phrase anywhere on the page.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN CONTAINS. grep over specs/ISO_COBOL.md finds five occurrences of the two phrases:
  13937  '\u23a2 feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2 ... \u23a5'   <- inside the fenced diagram, correct
  13938  '\u23a3 device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3 ... \u23a6'    <- inside the fenced diagram, correct
  13941  inline mentions within the '> **Figure notes ...**' blockquote  <- legitimate prose
  13944  '`feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2`'                    <- SPURIOUS
  13945  '`device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3`'                     <- SPURIOUS
Lines 13944-13945 are ordinary top-level lines (no '>' prefix, column 0), separated from the figure notes by a blank line and from '[ symbolic-characters-clause ] ...' (13947) by another blank line. They are therefore a third, structurally-positioned copy of content that the PDF prints once.

WHY THE STANDARD REFUTATIONS DO NOT APPLY.
  - Not missing text reflowed onto an adjacent line: the defect is EXTRA text, not missing text, and the fenced diagram already carries the correct copy.
  - Not page-break furniture: the whole format begins and ends on page 320; the slice is self-contained.
  - Not line wrapping or hyphenation: the strings are byte-identical duplicates, not a wrap of the fenced lines.
  - Not a transcription convention: this page's own convention is visible in the same slice - simple one-line clauses are rendered ONCE as a code span (line 13920 CURRENCY SIGN..., line 13928 LOCALE...), and complex ones ONCE as a fenced diagram plus figure notes (lines 13912-13916, 13930-13942). Nothing else on the page restates fenced content as a code span afterwards. There is no marker labelling 13944-13945 as a flattening or a restatement.
  - The claim does not misquote either source: I verified the PDF glyphs by magnified render and the markdown by raw grep with line numbers.

MEANING CHANGE. It is material. The correct reading, per ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.6 metalanguage and the figure notes at 13941, is one OPTIONAL, REPEATABLE bracketed clause offering three mutually exclusive alternatives (switch-name-1 form / feature-name-1 form / device-name-1 form). The stray lines 13944-13945 present the second and third alternatives as bare, unbracketed entries in the SPECIAL-NAMES clause sequence, sitting between the switch clause and [ symbolic-characters-clause ] ... . Because every genuine top-level clause on this page carries its own brackets, an unbracketed entry at that position reads as REQUIRED and NON-REPEATABLE, and as a SEPARATE clause that may co-occur with the switch clause rather than excluding it. A grammar generator walking the clause list would emit two extra mandatory productions and would lose the mutual exclusion. Severity 'structural' is correct.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, and the claim is accurate as written; two refinements for the record. (1) Occurrence count in the markdown is five, not four: besides the correct fenced copies at 13937-13938 and the spurious copies at 13944-13945, both phrases are also named inline inside the figure-notes blockquote at line 13941 ('it offers three alternatives - the `switch-name-1` form, `feature-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-2`, or `device-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-3`'). That prose mention is legitimate and must be kept; only 13944-13945 are spurious. (2) The two spurious lines are adjacent with no blank line between them, so Markdown renders them as a single paragraph with a soft break rather than two separate blocks - immaterial to the defect, but relevant if a downstream extractor splits on blank lines. FIX: delete lines 13944-13945 (and the now-redundant blank line), leaving the fenced diagram at 13930-13939 and its figure notes at 13941-13942 as the sole representation of the clause, so that '[ symbolic-characters-clause ] ...' follows the notes directly, exactly as printed on folio 290.
